## Latest continuation: an explicit measure and a Lean ordinary-series criterion

**Collatz remains OPEN.** This is a second pushed checkpoint after 273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff. The new Lean theorem proves an exact convergence criterion for every fixed positive integer. The universal finiteness bound, the global supersolution and the remaining marked-return estimate are unproved.

**Published head:** `a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e`  
**Tree:** `2174fa902c45c16b208cb5f129dcb5c987309050`  
**15 added files; 1,317 added lines.** All 38 files added across the two checkpoints were read back and matched at this final head.

[Latest scientific overview](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/continuation/README.md) · [Fixed biased measure and full ordinary criterion](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/continuation/BIASED_PARITY_MEASURE.md) · [Lean source](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/continuation/lean/BiasedParity.lean) · [Proper multiscale score](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/continuation/MULTISCALE_CLOSURE.md) · [Physical reset frequency](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/continuation/QUANTITATIVE_RESETS.md) · [Independent reconstruction](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/reports/2026-11-24-high-variance-closure/continuation/ROOT_REVIEW.md) · [Fresh execution receipt](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/a30402b7849c437edf245974d9f436d1f105e08e/reports/2026-11-24-high-variance-closure/continuation/REPLAY.json)

### 1. A fixed-source theorem, fully in Lean

For every positive ordinary n, put A_k(n)=2^(k+P_k(n))/3^k, where P_k counts its actual odd shortcut inputs. Lean proves:

- the sequence of A_k is bounded iff n reaches one;
- the series sum A_k converges iff n reaches one;
- on a high actual prefix, 2^(3k)(T^k n)^3 <= n^3 2^(5P_k);
- on any hypothetical nonconverger, A_k^5 >= (256/243)^k/n^3.

The positive base below 20 is locally kernel checked. The forward proof establishes summability after any finite actual hit of one. The measure with iid odd parity probability 2/3 is specified independently of termination; its written layer-sum identity identifies the same series with its exponential valuation potential. **Universal finiteness is not proved.**

The ordinary recurrences S(2n)=1+(2/3)S(n) and S(2n+1)=1+(4/3)S(3n+2) identify the missing finite nonnegative supersolution. For every finite set of primes, floor and binary prefix, the written construction gives nonintegral positive rationals passing those local tests, remaining above the floor and having infinite potential. These are explicitly not ordinary counterexamples.

### 2. A proper score with one remaining refill

Forward wrapping of sparse markers leaves only the highest active level able to refill. Virtual-start separation is proved even when a marker is witnessed by a different actual predecessor. This yields a computable proper integer toll b_* which never increases across a marked edge. With total actual hitting clocks t_l and summable weights, R_*=4 sum w_l t_l+W_1 b_* is finite and proper on every positive ordinary input.

At a nonperiodic marked source its exact debit is
4(W_(J+1)−w_J t_J(Tn))+W_1(b_*(n)−b_*(Tn)).
The latter term is nonnegative; no theorem pays the first return cost universally. At periodic sources the display is only an upper bound because additional finite-cycle kills can intervene. Those kills do not exclude a nontrivial cycle.

### 3. Actual reset counts, and continued tests of the candidate

A fixed-base two-logarithm estimate yields p>0 and a uniform bound O(sqrt(log n)(log n)^(-p)) on visits to the actual sparse reset image in each true sqrt(log n)-clock block. On a fixed escape the weighted reset cost remains negligible even when its relative toll grows as (log n)^delta for any delta<p. A potential realizing the displayed physical debit would force a finite global attractor; it is not constructed here. The reset-clock, simultaneous-section and centered sawtooth attempts include exact ordinary witnesses and preserve their first unsupported implication.

### Executed verification

The new module and its exact QuarterShift dependency were freshly compiled in an empty directory, with pinned Lean 4.34.1/Mathlib and warnings-as-errors. All five new public declaration audits and five dependency audits passed, with only standard axioms. **Across both checkpoints: six distinct Lean modules and 29 distinct public declarations audited.**

Two additional finite controls passed in normal and optimized Python. The measure construction, multiscale score, reset-frequency theorem and analytic candidate tests remain **written mathematics, not Lean formalizations**. No full-conjecture proof was compiled.

The final clean complete checkout passed all five default integrity commands, covering **789 tracked files**. Repository integrity is separate from mathematics.

## Previous checkpoint: an all-ordinary potential with sparse resets

**Collatz remains OPEN.** The high-variance continuation constructs a computable proper rank and a finite diffuse valuation potential on every positive odd input, with uniform debit outside one decidable density-zero reset section. Its debit through the resets remains unproved. A separate exact quarter-shift identity sharpens the ordinary atomic-moment target; the required ordinary contraction is also unproved.

**Published head:** `273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff`  
**Tree:** `7f95321004d0e9220dcecb95e912531d7ac4c33b`  
**23 added files; 2,289 added lines.** All 23 published files were read back and matched their local content.

[Scientific overview](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/README.md) · [All-ordinary sparse-reset construction](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/SPARSE_RESET_MEASURE.md) · [Quarter shift and exact closing estimate](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/QUARTER_SHIFT.md) · [Whole inverse-tree comparison](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff/research/high-variance-closure-20261124/RESTRICTED_RANK.md) · [Root review](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff/reports/2026-11-24-high-variance-closure/ROOT_REVIEW.md) · [Fresh scoped replay](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/273e5433a4b16a17998ad98d92549ee06896abff/reports/2026-11-24-high-variance-closure/REPLAY.json)

### What changed mathematically

- **Diffuse representability and an unconditional construction.** Every proper integer ordinary rank can be approximated by a singular continuous valuation potential or an L1-density potential of arbitrarily small total mass. A finite actual phase selector then constructs such a rank on every positive odd input, including hypothetical outsiders, with uniform debit away from a fixed sparse marked set. The actual reset 7→13 defeats an unrestricted debit.
- **Optimal bounded quarter correction.** The identity T(n)+1/4 = (3^(n mod 2)/2)(n+1/2) gives parity-independent killing. The bound liminf I_k(3/2)^(1/k) < (81/82)^(3/2) ≈ 0.9817632 would settle all Collatz, using the locally kernel-checked base below 20. The Haar rate ≈0.9659258 has not been transferred to the ordinary trace. The 1/4 additive defect is optimal among bounded coordinate changes even within one fixed predecessor basin.
- **The full previously open restricted envelope increases.** E(31)≤18<128/7≤E(121) on the actual valley 31→121, with an infinite-tree tail bound. This is a strict comparison of real suprema, not just of chosen centers. A nonlinear repair is nonincreasing but fails to yield a strict well-founded return. A source-qualified real/dyadic antipode criterion exposes the remaining Diophantine power-gain requirement.
- **Ordinary boundary rigidity and finite clock obstruction.** Persistent boundary addresses have Hausdorff dimension at most 1/2, with exact oriented ternary transfers and explicit new-boundary creation. On the four-trit head there are ≫X^(1−c) pairs with no meeting by independent clocks (1+b)log2 X for 0<b<c<0.16. This does not give permanent failures.
- **Latest-source overlap retained.** PR192 at 045be43632f274dd64faf15714e42cc8de27a2e9 already supplies overlapping odd-clock moment and killed-test reductions. They are credited. PR197/146 inputs and the latest PR199/200 intake are pinned without importing unverified external or draft-Lean claims.

### What was actually checked

Five exact Lean sources were freshly compiled in separate empty build directories, with Lean 4.34.1 and pinned Mathlib, warnings treated as errors. **All 24 named transitive axiom audits passed**, with only standard Lean axioms. Four finite Python controls passed in normal and optimized modes with identical output. The measure, analytic, minimax, real-address and asymptotic claims remain **written mathematics, not Lean formalizations**. The external 2^71 verification floor was not replayed.

The complete clean checkout at the exact published commit passed all five default integrity commands, covering 774 tracked files. This checks repository integrity separately from mathematics.

Lean proves `collatz_iff_residual_marked`. The written density calculation covers `16/31` of marks in an asymptotic dyadic octave. The residual convergence obligation is not assumed.

Combining this checked marked descent with PR193's **written** translated-interval synchronization yields an explicit **decidable** set S of marked integers with

```text
Collatz holds iff every member of S reaches 1,
sum_(n in S) n^(-theta) < infinity,
theta = H_2(log 2 / log 3) = 0.9499555...
```
